docs.title: Welcome to my homelab documentation
docs.text:
This is the third version of my homelab

v1 : Personnal-docker-config v2 : Homelab-infra v3 : homelabv3-infra

To start, I would like to thank all maintainers and contributors to open source projects that make my lab possible !

docs.title: What are the key features
docs.text:
• Open source
  • Dual stacks IPv4/IPv6
  • Privacy
  • Security
  • PKI with certificates autorenew
  • Monitoring, logging and alerting
  • Offsite encrypted backup to S3 multi A-Z
  • Manage everything except :
  • Emails
  • Eveything is automated with scripts, IaC, etc except :
  • Networking hardware device configuration (routers, switchs)

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
Install git and clone the project 

apt install -y git
git clone https://github.com/M0NsTeRRR/homelabv3-infra.git

Warning

This guide assumes the following :

  • You have configured an SSH agent with your SSH keys
  • You have ghcr.io configured with a github token (needed for OCI helm chart) with Public Repositories (read-only) access (cat ~/github_token.txt | docker login ghcr.io -u m0nsterrr --password-stdin)

docs.title: with devenv recommended
docs.text:
1. Follow devenv documentation to install it
  2. Open a devenv shell devenv shell

docs.title: Guide
docs.text: The following guides demonstrate use-cases and provide examples of how to use the project.

docs.title: What is Ansible ?
docs.text: Ansible gives the ability to do software provisioning, configuration management, and application deployment functionality. It will allow us to deploy generic configuration to Packer template and applications.

docs.title: Execute
docs.text:
Configuration is stored in ansible folder.

Fill ssl folders with certificates. Fill .vault_password.txt at root with ansible vault password used.

uv run task ansible:<openbao|generate_certs>

docs.text: • Github actions

docs.title: DNS Blocklist
docs.text: In addition to uBlock Origins for Firefox , some devices, such as the YouTube app on my Android TV, do not use Firefox, so I've added a DNS blocklist to restrict trackers.

docs.title: What is Flux ?
docs.text: Flux is a declarative, GitOps continuous delivery tool for Kubernetes.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Configuration is stored in kubernetes folder.

Nothing to do, configuration is deployed in the cluster from the Git repository.

docs.title: What is IncusOS ?
docs.text: IncusOS is an immutable OS solely designed around safely and reliably running Incus. Incus is a next-generation system container, application container, and virtual machine manager.

docs.title: Install IncusOS
docs.text:
1. Go to the IncusOS image downloader.
  2. In installation target Wipe the target drive must be checked.
  3. In target drive identifier, put wwn
  4. In application configuration Apply default configuration must be checked only for server1.
  5. In TLS client certificate copy the output of incus remote get-client-certificate
  6. In the advanced settings, paste the network configuration from incusos/serverX/network.yaml (where X represents the server number).
  7. Download the ISO.
  8. Configure the BIOS.
  9. Boot from the ISO.
  10. Install and reboot
  11. Connect to IncusOS

docs.title: Post install setup
docs.text:
Add the remote server 

incus remote add serverX serverX.unicornafk.fr

Retrieve encryption recovery key in OS > System > Security

Create Volumes 

# Volumes
incus storage volume create local flatcar

Create Networks 

incus network create prod parent=enp3s0 vlan=10 --type=physical
incus network create lab parent=enp3s0 vlan=20 --type=physical

docs.title: Add custom CA certs
docs.text: https://linuxcontainers.org/incus-os/docs/main/reference/system/security/#configuration-options

docs.title: Configure ACME
docs.text:
In OS > System > Security add custom CA cert. 

custom_ca_certs:
  - |
    -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
    xxxxxxx

In settings page configure the following :

acme.agree_tos: true acme.ca_url: https://openbao.unicornafk.fr:8200/v1/pki/acme/directory acme.domain: server.unicornafk.fr,serverX.unicornafk.fr (where X represents the server number) acme.email: admin@unicornafk.fr

docs.text: Kubernetes also known as K8s, is an open source system for automating deployment, scaling, and management of containerized applications.

docs.title: What is Octodns ?
docs.text: Octodns gives the ability to manage DNS agnostically across multiple providers.

docs.title: Internal
docs.text:
Configuration is stored in octodns/internal folder.

MIKROTIK_USER and MIKROTIK_PASSWORD represent the username and password used to connect to your MikroTik router to manage your DNS zone.

export MIKROTIK_USER=<MIKROTIK_USER>
export MIKROTIK_PASSWORD=<MIKROTIK_PASSWORD>
uv run task octodns:sync-internal

docs.title: External
docs.text:
You should not normally use it by hand it's running in a Github action.

Configuration is stored in octodns/external folder.

INFOMANIAK_TOKEN represents the API token to manage your DNS zone

export INFOMANIAK_TOKEN=<INFOMANIAK_TOKEN>
uv run task octodns:sync-external

docs.title: What is Renovatebot ?
docs.text: Renovatebot is an universal dependency update tool that fits into your workflows.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Configuration is stored in .github/renovate.json5 file.

Install the Github application in your git repository

Nothing more to do, the application use the configuration from the Git repository.

docs.title: ACL for backup bucket
docs.text:
Replace <bucket_name> in the json below.

{
    "Version": "2012-10-17",
    "Statement": [
        {
            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Action": [
                "s3:*"
            ],
            "Resource": [
                "arn:aws:s3:::<bucket_name>/*"
            ]
        }
    ]
}

docs.title: snmp-exporter
docs.text: SNMP Exporter this exporter is the recommended way to expose SNMP data in a format which Prometheus can ingest.

docs.title: How to generate snmp-exporter configuration ?
docs.text:
SNMP v3 must be enabled and configured on all devices.

Download the mib files :

  • Mikrotik mib
  • Brocade
  • Qnap : Go to Control Panel > Network & File Services > SNMP and Under SNMP MIB, click Download.

Don't forget to change in the following configuration :

  • <snmp_exporter_username>
  • <snmp_exporter_pass>
  • <snmp_exporter_private>
snmp-generator.yml
---
auths:
  homelab_aes:
    version: 3
    username: "<snmp_exporter_username>"
    password: "<snmp_exporter_pass>"
    security_level: authPriv
    auth_protocol: SHA
    priv_protocol: AES
    priv_password: "<snmp_exporter_private>"
  homelab_des:
    version: 3
    username: "<snmp_exporter_username>"
    password: "<snmp_exporter_pass>"
    security_level: authPriv
    auth_protocol: SHA
    priv_protocol: DES
    priv_password: "<snmp_exporter_private>"
modules:
  # Default IF-MIB interfaces table with ifIndex.
  if_mib:
    walk:
      - 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.3 # sysUpTime
      - 1.3.6.1.2.1.2 # interfaces
      - 1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1 # ifXTable
    lookups:
      - source_indexes: [ifIndex]
        lookup: ifAlias
      - source_indexes: [ifIndex]
        lookup: ifDescr
      - source_indexes: [ifIndex]
        lookup: 1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1.1.1

  # Mikrotik CCR2004-1g-12s+2xs
  mikrotik:
    walk:
      - 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.3 # sysUpTime
      - 1.3.6.1.2.1.2 # interfaces
      - 1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1 # ifXTable
      - 1.3.6.1.4.1.14988 # mikrotik
    lookups:
      - source_indexes: [ifIndex]
        lookup: ifAlias
      - source_indexes: [ifIndex]
        lookup: ifDescr
      - source_indexes: [ifIndex]
        lookup: 1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1.1.1

  # Brocade ICX 6450-24P & ICX 7150-C12P
  brocade:
    walk:
      - 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.3 # sysUpTime
      - 1.3.6.1.2.1.2 # interfaces
      - 1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1 # ifXTable
      - 1.3.6.1.4.1.1991.1.1.2.1.11 # snAgImgVer
      - 1.3.6.1.4.1.1991.1.1.1.2 # snChasPwr
      - 1.3.6.1.4.1.1991.1.1.1.3 # snChasFan
      - 1.3.6.1.4.1.1991.1.1.2.11 # snAgentCpu
      - 1.3.6.1.4.1.1991.1.1.2.1.53 # snAgentMemUtil
      - 1.3.6.1.4.1.1991.1.1.2.13 # snAgentTemp
    lookups:
      - source_indexes: [ifIndex]
        lookup: ifAlias
      - source_indexes: [ifIndex]
        lookup: ifDescr
      - source_indexes: [ifIndex]
        lookup: 1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1.1.1

Follow instructions step from snmp-exporter documentation

Configure snmp-exporter config to use the appropriate crendentials

docs.title: What is Truenas ?
docs.text: Truenas is a family of network-attached storage (NAS) products produced by iXsystems, incorporating both FOSS, as well as commercial offerings.

docs.title: ACME DNS Challenge with vault PKI and PDNS
docs.text:
1. Create a dataset (home directories can't execute scripts see here)
  2. Select an user and create an API Key for it
  3. Connect to truenas through SSH with your user and execute every action with it (do not use root) and move inside your new dataset
  4. Clone acme.sh git clone https://github.com/acmesh-official/acme.sh .acme.sh
  5. Create an env file /home/<user>/.acme.sh.env with the below contents
# PDNS
PDNS_Url=<TO_REPLACE>
PDNS_ServerId=localhost
PDNS_Token=<TO_REPLACE>
PDNS_Ttl=60
# PKI CA
CA_CERT_PATH=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
# Truenas
DEPLOY_TRUENAS_APIKEY=<TO_REPLACE>
DEPLOY_TRUENAS_SCHEME=https
  1. Change your current directory to acme.sh project cd .acme.sh
  2. Register ACME server ./acme.sh --set-default-ca --server <vault_acme_url> --home /home/admin (in my case https://openbao.unicornafk.fr:8200/v1/pki/acme/directory)
  3. Register DNS issuer ./acme.sh --issue --insecure --dns dns_pdns -d <truenas_fqdn> --dnssleep 30 --home /home/admin
  4. Deploy the certificate ./acme.sh -d <truenas_fqdn> --insecure --deploy --deploy-hook truenas --home /home/admin

  5. Setup cron through the webui

  6. Description: ACME.Sh renew certificates

  7. User: <user>
  8. Schedule: Daily

  9. Command: . /home/<user>/.acme.sh.env && "<dataset path>/.acme.sh"/acme.sh --issue --dns dns_pdns -d <truenas_fqdn> --dnssleep 30 --insecure --deploy --deploy-hook truenas --ca-bundle /home/admin/ca.crt --home /home/admin

  10. If you want to check if your cron is successfull run it and check the log with

cat /var/log/syslog | grep -w 'cron'

!! info "sudo is broken https://ixsystems.atlassian.net/browse/NAS-131540"

docs.text:

  • unicornafk.fr for internal services

docs.title: Cloud providers
docs.text:
• Infomaniak for registrar, authoritative DNS and for S3
  • Hurricane Electric for secondary DNS
  • Proton for emails and VPN
  • Oracle for VPS

docs.title: Choices
docs.text: On this page, I will explain some choices I made as an F.A.Q

docs.title: Why do I use cloud services ?
docs.text:
• Email system is a headhache (blacklist/whitelist etc...) and I don't want to invest time into it
  • Offsite backup (s3 buckets)
  • Disaster recovery, offsite monitoring

docs.title: Why did I choose T-bao MN58U as a server ?
docs.text: I've replaced my old servers (R320, Homemade with R7 2700) to reduce electricity costs. This server uses only 15W to operate. It is small and doesn't make any noises, and it still has a pretty decent processor with 32Gb RAM.

docs.title: Why I'm using cloud european services ?
docs.text: My conviction regarding GAFAM and GDPR.

docs.title: Why do I have an Oracle VPS ?
docs.text: Because this VPS is completely Free with disk encryption otherwise I would have used probably Hetzner like in the past.
